title: R' Mansya, grandson of R' Musya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R' Mansya, grandson of R' Musya.
He is mentioned in [Yoma 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.4b.11) according to the reading Hyman attributes to Sheiltot, Va’etchanan.
He said in the name of R' Mansya the Great. In [Midrash Tehillim](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.1.17), R' Mansya says, ‘A counsel containing the word of the Lord will stand.’

notes.text: The supplied Yoma locator ר: would ordinarily mean 200b and is unresolved. The heading gives a grandson of Rabbi Musya; it does not identify him with Rabbi Mansya the Great.

The saved whole Davidson Yoma4b scalar has the parenthesized Musya, grandson of Masya, reporting Musya, with Rabbah after the parenthesis. This is a matching saying beside supplied ר:, conventionally200b, not proof that printed dalet became resh or that a historical deletion occurred. Hyman’s Mansya/grandson-of-Musya/Mansya-the-Great chain is retained separately. The SheiltotVaetchanan attribution was not newly inspected, and EinYaakov/SederHaDorot search leads are not full primary witnesses. Hyman’s MidrashTehillim quote is retained without adding a section or identity. Unverified Mansya/Musya title expansions remain R'.

[Hyman’s printed page](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=61) reads Yoma 4b, while the supplied Hebrew gives ר:. The Gemara has Musya, grandson of Masya. The Hebrew in [Ein Yaakov](https://www.sefaria.org/Ein_Yaakov_(Glick_Edition)%2C_Yoma.1.4) has Mansya, grandson of Mansya, and [Sheiltot 28 in Vayeshev](https://www.sefaria.org/Sheiltot_d'Rav_Achai_Gaon.28.1) has Mansya son of Mansya. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2514&lang=en) records differing forms. Hyman cites Va’etchanan, whose exact witness remains unverified. The linked Midrash names Rabbi Manshia for the saying about counsel.
